title: How to Wash Cashmere

seo.title: How to Wash Cashmere
seo.meta_description: Wash cashmere according to its label using cool or lukewarm water, wool-safe detergent, and minimal friction; do not wring and dry flat.
seo.search_intent: Wash cashmere garments without shrinking, felting, stretching, or distorting the fibers during washing and drying.

excerpt: Cashmere does not need aggressive cleaning; it needs control of friction, temperature, and weight while wet. The care label determines whether home washing is appropriate.
content_html:
Read the care label before getting cashmere wet. If it calls for professional cleaning, follow that instruction; if washing is allowed, treat the garment as very delicate wool.

Use stable cool or lukewarm water

Avoid sudden temperature changes. Dissolve a small amount of wool- or delicate-safe detergent before adding the garment.

Press and swish gently instead of rubbing

Move the garment slowly through the water. Do not brush, wring, or scrub sections against each other; moisture, heat, and friction encourage felting.

Rinse without stretching

Support the garment’s weight as you change water. Do not lift a saturated sweater by one sleeve or shoulder.

Remove water with a towel

Lay the garment flat, roll it gently in a clean towel, and press. Then reshape the shoulders, sleeves, and edges to their original dimensions.

Dry flat

Wet cashmere can stretch under its own weight, so avoid hanging it. Keep it away from intense direct heat and tumble drying unless the label specifically allows a method.

Surface pilling does not necessarily mean the garment is dirty. Remove pills only when dry with a tool intended for knitwear, taking care not to thin the fabric.

faq.question: Can cashmere go in the washing machine?
faq.answer: Only when the care label permits it and you use the recommended delicate or wool program.

faq.question: Why should I avoid wringing it?
faq.answer: Friction and distortion of wet fibers can cause felting and loss of shape.

faq.question: Should cashmere be hung to dry?
faq.answer: Usually no. Drying flat helps prevent the weight of the wet garment from stretching it.
